title: Adding and removing edges and vertices in an adjacency matrix
summary: Demonstrate adding and removing edges and vertices in an adjacency matrix, distinguishing cell updates from full row and column insertions or deletions.
context: The order of vertex list V maps to row and column indices of the matrix, and the table headers show both index and vertex ID. An entry of 1 at M[i,j] indicates an edge between V[i] and V[j], whereas 0 indicates no edge.
description: An undirected edge connects two vertices, so adding or removing an edge updates both symmetric positions M[i,j] and M[j,i] together. Each frame's state table lists the complete matrix after that step finishes.

Adding a vertex appends a row and a column of all 0s at the end of the matrix; removing a vertex deletes its entire row and column, decrementing the matrix indices of subsequent vertices while leaving each vertex's own identity and name unchanged.

frames.title: Initialize the five-vertex graph
frames.explanation: Initially, V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] corresponds to indices 0 through 4, forming a 5×5 matrix. The 6 undirected edges 1—3, 1—5, 2—3, 2—5, 2—4, and 4—5 each appear as a symmetric pair of 1s; edge 1—2 does not yet exist.
frames.key_state: Initial state: V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] at indices 0 through 4, 5×5 matrix with 6 edges; M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 0, with no edge 1—2 yet.
frames.announcement: Initial state: V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] at indices 0 through 4, 5×5 matrix with 6 edges; M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 0, with no edge 1—2 yet.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix step 1: Complete initial state

frames.title: Add edge 1—2
frames.explanation: Vertices 1 and 2 correspond to indices 0 and 2. Adding edge 1—2 changes M[0,2] and M[2,0] from 0 to 1 while leaving all other cells unchanged; the matrix remains 5×5 with 7 edges in total.
frames.key_state: State after adding 1—2: V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], 5×5 matrix with 7 edges; M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 1.
frames.announcement: Vertices 1 and 2 correspond to indices 0 and 2. Adding edge 1—2 changes M[0,2] and M[2,0] from 0 to 1 while leaving all other cells unchanged; the matrix remains 5×5 with 7 edges in total.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix step 2: Complete state after adding edge 1—2

frames.title: Remove edge 1—3
frames.explanation: Vertices 1 and 3 correspond to indices 0 and 1. Removing edge 1—3 changes M[0,1] and M[1,0] from 1 to 0 while leaving all other cells unchanged; the matrix remains 5×5, retaining 6 edges including 1—2.
frames.key_state: State after removing 1—3: V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4], 5×5 matrix with 6 edges; M[0,1] and M[1,0] are 0, while 1—2 remains.
frames.announcement: Vertices 1 and 3 correspond to indices 0 and 1. Removing edge 1—3 changes M[0,1] and M[1,0] from 1 to 0 while leaving all other cells unchanged; the matrix remains 5×5, retaining 6 edges including 1—2.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix step 3: Complete state after removing edge 1—3

frames.title: Add isolated vertex 6
frames.explanation: Append isolated vertex 6 to V, giving V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6] at new index 5. The matrix expands to 6×6 with the new row and column filled with 0s and all other cells unchanged; the edge count stays 6.
frames.key_state: State after adding isolated vertex 6: V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6], 6×6 matrix with 6 edges; vertex 6 is at index 5 with its row and column all 0.
frames.announcement: Append isolated vertex 6 to V, giving V = [1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6] at new index 5. The matrix expands to 6×6 with the new row and column filled with 0s and all other cells unchanged; the edge count stays 6.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix step 4: Complete state after adding isolated vertex 6

frames.title: Remove vertex 3
frames.explanation: Delete the entire row and column for vertex 3 (former index 1), simultaneously removing its sole remaining incident edge 2—3; edge 1—3 was already removed in step 3. V becomes [1, 2, 5, 4, 6] at indices 0 through 4, shrinking the matrix to 5×5 with 5 edges in total. The indices of vertices 2, 5, 4, 6 each decrease by 1 without renaming any vertex—for example, vertex 2 shifts from index 2 to 1. Vertex 6 is now at index 4 with all 0s in its row and column, remaining isolated.
frames.key_state: State after removing vertex 3: V = [1, 2, 5, 4, 6] at indices 0 through 4, 5×5 matrix with 5 edges; vertex 2 is now at index 1 with its identity unchanged, and vertex 6 is at index 4 with its row and column all 0.
frames.announcement: Delete former index 1's row and column for vertex 3 along with incident edge 2—3. V = [1, 2, 5, 4, 6], shrinking the matrix to 5×5 with 5 edges; vertex 2 moves to index 1 without changing names, and 6 stays isolated.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix step 5: Complete state after removing vertex 3
